Dana H.: Heads up: Meridian Health wants a short POC for Private deployment. NetSec asks for a strict allowlist and whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is recommended given they run TLS inspection. Need a short, copy-pasteable ask list.
Omar R.: PrivateLink is our default for cross-account gov customers. Pros: minimal routing changes, smaller blast radius. Cons: ENI source IPs are used once traffic leaves their VPC (so DPS/IDS may see different src).
Kavi P.: If they require original source IP for DPI/DLP, peering/TGW is preferable (no NAT). Also confirm CIDR overlap and routes.
NetBot: Snapshot for thread 3478901234: ENI_IPS=["10.4.22.5","10.4.22.9"], NLB_EIPS=["34.215.11.9"], PORTS=["443"].
Sofia L.: Short ask list to send to Meridian NetSec: 1) Confirm AWS partition (aws vs aws-us-gov). 2) Choose mode (PrivateLink or Peering). 3a) If PrivateLink: share VPC ID, subnets, and security contact; we will provide ENI IPs. 3b) If Peering: share VPC CIDRs, on-prem egress IPs, and route tables. 4) TLS inspection: yes/no + vendor. 5) Cert model: customer CA or Redwood-managed.
Dana H.: Great. I'll send this and attach the NetBot snapshot. Omar/Kavi can you help with a one-page cert flow bullet list for their security team?
Omar R.: On it. Kavi can add ops caveats about TLS intercept.
Kavi P.: Will do, will flag that app-level mTLS may break if TLS inspection is inline.
